# Fixtures

| Directory | Contents |
|---|---|
| `sample/` | a small project written for the tests |
| `functions/` | a small project that uses functions of `.emet` of every kind, a keyword and a variable argument, a filter, `File.read` of a TSV and a tail recursion; built by the determinism check ([docs/adr/0162](../../../../docs/adr/0162-calling-emet-functions-from-gm.md)) |
| `emet-samples/` | a library of twenty functions of `.emet` an editor or an operator of a Japanese book would use (prices, kansuji, the Japanese era, ruby, a glossary and a table from TSV, filters for first-occurrence ruby, variant spellings and full-width letters), split by theme under `fn/`, with a chapter that calls each; the golem-driver test `EmetSamplesSpec` checks what each gives, and the determinism check builds it |
| `figures/` | a small project with an SVG, a PDF and a JPEG figure, for the goldens of the PDF and the EPUB (`OutputGoldenSpec`); the test copies its fonts in as `fonts/ja.otf` and `fonts/latin.otf` |
| `complex-vertical/` | a book that combines the features on a vertical page of one column (B6): ruby, kenten, tate-chu-yoko, notes, SVG, PNG, wrapped and turned figures, tables, code blocks, rules of headings and paragraphs, the contents, the index in two columns, the bibliography, functions and a filter of `.emet` ([docs/adr/0175](../../../../docs/adr/0175-complex-typesetting-fixture.md)); see "The two books that combine the features" |
| `complex-horizontal/` | the same on a horizontal page of two columns (A5), with notes at the foot of a column, figures fitted to a column, hyphenated Latin words and the index in three columns ([docs/adr/0175](../../../../docs/adr/0175-complex-typesetting-fixture.md)) |
| `conformance/` | a small book with every element of the structure tree of a tagged PDF: headings, nested lists, a definition list, a table across pages, a code block with a caption and line numbers, notes, a sidenote, external links, the contents, the index and the bibliography; set horizontally with `manifest.toml` and `style.toml`, and vertically, its notes at the end of the chapter and without the chapter of the sidenote, with `manifest-vertical.toml` and `style-vertical.toml`. `scripts/ci/conformance-pdfs.sh` declares PDF/A-2a and PDF/UA-1 for the CI job verapdf, and `TaggedPdfSpec` fixes its structure trees ([docs/adr/0183](../../../../docs/adr/0183-tagged-pdf-and-pdf-a.md)); the test copies its fonts in as `fonts/ja.otf` and `fonts/latin.otf` |
| `languages/` | a small horizontal book of the characters of both scripts (quotation marks, dashes, the ellipsis, guillemets) in and out of `[lang]` spans, `@lang` on blocks and its body form, and the hyphenation of English and French paragraphs; `TaggedPdfSpec` fixes its structure tree, `scripts/ci/conformance-pdfs.sh` declares PDF/A-2a and PDF/UA-1 for the CI job verapdf, and the visual regression test builds it ([docs/adr/0187](../../../../docs/adr/0187-inline-language-switch.md)); the tests copy its fonts in as `fonts/ja.otf` and `fonts/latin.otf` |
| `tempest/` | *The Tempest* by William Shakespeare, set horizontally |
| `kanikosen/` | 『蟹工船』小林多喜二, set vertically |
| `pd/` | ten public-domain books that are hard to set ([docs/adr/0026](../../../../docs/adr/0026-ten-public-domain-fixtures.md)) |

`tempest/tempest.gm`, `kanikosen/kanikosen.gm` and the `.gm` of every book
of `pd/` are generated by `scripts/fixtures/fetch-public-domain.sh`, which
downloads the texts, checks their SHA-256, converts them with
`golem-fixtures` (the converters in `modules/golem-fixtures`, run through
`cabal run`;
[docs/adr/0023](../../../../docs/adr/0023-fixture-converters-without-python.md),
[docs/adr/0026](../../../../docs/adr/0026-ten-public-domain-fixtures.md)) and
formats them with `golem fmt`.
Do not edit them by hand. To make them again:

```sh
GOLEM=$(cabal list-bin golem) scripts/fixtures/fetch-public-domain.sh
```

The source texts are not committed.

## The two books that combine the features

`complex-vertical/` and `complex-horizontal/` fix the interactions between
the features of Golem
([docs/adr/0175](../../../../docs/adr/0175-complex-typesetting-fixture.md)).
Their manuscripts are written by hand for this purpose (the vertical book is
a short Japanese essay on a letterpress shop, the horizontal one a short
technical book on a build tool); they are not converted from other texts.

They are two books, not one, because the writing mode is one for a whole
book (`writing-mode` of `[page]`) and because a wrapped figure cannot be
set on a page of two columns or more (G07026): the vertical book has one
column and a wrapped figure, the horizontal one two columns and none.
Neither has sidenotes, which no vertical page and no page of columns can
hold (G07001). Each book is 16 to 24 pages.

Both use: three levels of numbered headings with `rule-before` and
`rule-after`; a paragraph style with rules, with a paragraph split at the
end of a page or a column; running heads with the number and the title of
the chapter, and folios; `@toc`; mono and group ruby and kenten, in
headings too; footnotes with `[notes.rule]` and a `[cite ...]` in a
footnote; an SVG figure and a PNG or JPEG figure with figure numbers,
`[ref-number]` and `[ref-title]`; a figure that does not wrap with a
`width` (`12zw` in the vertical book, `60%` in the horizontal one,
docs/adr/0190); a table from a file and one written in
the manuscript, split at the end of a page or a column; `@listing` and code
blocks with wrapped lines, split at the end of a page or a column; a
numbered and a definition list; index marks of two levels, in a heading, a
footnote and a table cell; `@bibliography` of CSL-JSON; an inline and a
block function of `.emet` (the block one reads a TSV with `File.read` and
makes a table), and a filter of `[[filters]]` that puts kenten on the
first heading of each chapter, which the contents and the running heads
show. The vertical book also has `[tcy: ...]`, `[number-text ... style=tcy]`,
a wrapped figure followed by a paragraph with rules, a turned figure
(`rotate=true`) and a double dash; the horizontal book notes at the foot of
a column, figures fitted to a column and hyphenated Latin words. The
golem-driver test `ComplexFixtureSpec` checks that the sources still use
each of these.

Neither book gives a diagnostic on any target. Two features always give a
notice, a wrapped line of a code block (G07030) and a paragraph with rules
split across pages or columns (G07046), so each manifest silences these two
codes and no other. `ComplexFixtureSpec` checks that the table `[diagnostics]`
of each manifest has the one key `silence-notices = ["G07030", "G07046"]`
(docs/adr/0198). The PDF and the EPUB of each book are goldens of
`OutputGoldenSpec` (`test/golden/pdf-complex-*.txt` and
`epub-complex-*.txt`); `scripts/determinism.sh`, `scripts/env-determinism/check.sh`
and the visual regression test (`scripts/visual/build.sh`) build them too.
A pull request that writes their goldens or references again says in its
description which pages changed and why (`CONTRIBUTING.md`).

The fonts are not committed. The tests and the scripts copy Noto Serif JP
of `kanikosen/fonts/` and Source Sans Pro of golem-font in as
`fonts/ja.otf` and `fonts/latin.otf`, as for `figures/`. To build a book by
hand:

```sh
cd modules/golem-driver/test/fixtures/complex-vertical
mkdir -p fonts
cp ../kanikosen/fonts/NotoSerifJP-Regular.otf fonts/ja.otf
cp ../../../../golem-font/test/fonts/SourceSansPro-Regular.otf fonts/latin.otf
golem build
```

`fonts/` and `build/` are ignored by git.

## Sources

- *The Tempest*: Project Gutenberg eBook #23042, the Cambridge edition
  (1863) edited by W. G. Clark and W. A. Wright. The play is in the public
  domain. The converter drops the Project Gutenberg header and licence,
  the transcriber's note, the footnotes and the textual notes; the result
  carries no Project Gutenberg trademark. Verse is set with `@style verse`. The
  source marks verse only by its line breaks, so the converter guesses it
  and takes a few short prose speeches whose lines all start with capitals
  for verse (two in Act I, Scene I).
- 『蟹工船』: 青空文庫 図書カード No.1465（底本「蟹工船・党生活者」新潮文庫）。
  著作権の保護期間は満了している。入力者、校正者と底本の情報は、青空文庫の
  ファイルにあるとおり `kanikosen.gm` の末尾に残している。

## The ten books of `pd/`

Each book is a Golem project like the two above: the English books are set
horizontally on A5 in Source Serif, the Japanese books vertically on B6 in
Noto Serif JP, with the page grids of *The Tempest* and 『蟹工船』.
All ten are in the public domain in Japan and in the United States: every
author and translator died before 1968 (the Japanese term of fifty years
after death, extended for the nationals of the Allied Powers, ran out
before the term became seventy years on 2018-12-30), and every work was
published before 1931. The Project Gutenberg header and licence are
dropped (the result carries no Project Gutenberg trademark); the Aozora
Bunko colophon, with its typists, proofreaders and base edition, is kept
at the end of each Japanese book.

### What the converters do not carry over

- `merry-wives`: `gutenberg-play` is the converter of *The Tempest*, unchanged
  (docs/adr/0023). In the list of characters, the braces that group two
  or three names are kept as `}` without their columns, and the
  footnote of the list and the title (`THE` / `MERRY WIVES OF WINDSOR.`)
  become items of the list.
- `frogs`: the source wraps some long lines of verse in the middle; a line
  is joined to the one before only when that one is 66 characters or
  longer and the line starts in lowercase, so some wraps remain.
  Stage directions in italic that span several blocks are italic only in
  the first.
- `snark`: the centred title lines are not centred (a paragraph style has no
  alignment); the contents list is kept as lines of verse.
- `elements-of-style`: the two columns become a table with an empty header
  row. The contents list loses its page-number column (each entry becomes a
  quotation ending with the page number). The word list of "Words often
  misspelled" (one word per line) becomes one paragraph.
- `nightmare-abbey`: Greek is transliterated in the source
  (`[Greek: philoschios]`) and stays so. The names of the speakers of the
  dialogues are paragraphs of their own, as in the source.
  No passage is marked as French or Latin, so they are hyphenated with
  the English patterns.
- Aozora Bunko (all five): gaiji given only by a JIS X 0213 plane-row-cell
  number, without a Unicode code point, become `〓` (6 in 高野聖, 7 in 一握の
  砂, 2 in 春と修羅, 14 in 平将門). 傍線, 地付き and 地からの字上げ,
  行右小書き, 段階の小さな文字 and ページの左右中央 are dropped and the text
  kept. Kaeriten and the okurigana of kunten are small characters in the
  line (`[style kunten: …]`), not at the lower left of the kanji. 同行見出し
  become bold.

## Fonts

Each book of the two above carries its fonts under `fonts/`, with their
licences, so the fixture builds as it is (`golem build` in its directory).

- `kanikosen/fonts/NotoSerifJP-Regular.otf`: Noto Serif CJK JP 2.003, the
  Japanese subset OTF from https://github.com/notofonts/noto-cjk (release
  `Serif2.003`, `12_NotoSerifJP.zip`), SHA-256
  `2c9a12dbd4f2408c4610c7ee84a108b62d7236c3775baed618c64d9cb44b2f04`.
  SIL Open Font License 1.1.
- `tempest/fonts/SourceSerifVariable-Roman.ttf`: Source Serif, the test
  font of golem-font (variable; Golem uses its default instance).
  SIL Open Font License 1.1.

The ten books of `pd/` do not commit their fonts (`.gitignore`), to keep
34 MB of copies out of the repository. `scripts/fixtures/copy-fonts.sh`
copies the fonts and licences of `kanikosen/` into the Japanese books and
those of `tempest/` into the English ones; `fetch-public-domain.sh` runs it.

```sh
scripts/fixtures/copy-fonts.sh
cd modules/golem-driver/test/fixtures/pd/koya-hijiri && golem build
```

## Tests

The golem-driver tests check each book of `pd/` without errors (as
`golem check` does). With `GOLEM_PD_BOOKS=1` (only `1`; `0` or `yes` is as
if unset), they build every target of each book, check the PDF with qpdf
and its writing mode; this takes about 35 seconds for the ten. Without it,
the suite ends with a line of how many books were checked only.

```sh
GOLEM_PD_BOOKS=1 cabal test golem-driver --test-options='-p 0026'
```
